report.root_cause: The lb admin/stats listener is likely blocked in its serial client-handling loop: a blocking read on one accepted connection prevents accepting the next admin client, consistent with the failed probe; no triggering commit or config change is observed.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Recent lb.conf change directly caused the failure

ranked.root_cause: The lb stats/admin loop serially blocks reading accepted clients, which can stall subsequent admin probes; trigger is unconfirmed.
The lb process may be overloaded or resource-constrained; metrics are insufficient to establish this.
Host-level resource contention may be affecting lb responsiveness; no confirming resource trend is available.

findings.question: Does the current lb source contain a defect or coupling that can make the admin/stats endpoint unresponsive while data traffic continues?
findings.summary: [code file=load-balancer/LoadBalancer.cpp smell=blocking-single-client-stats-handler tests=fail] The stats endpoint can become unresponsive while data traffic continues: its dedicated thread accepts one client and performs a blocking read before it can accept another, while the separate main accept loop enqueues data clients independently. A stats client that connects without sending data can therefore tie up stats service without stopping data handling. I would use bounded/nonblocking reads and writes or dispatch stats clients to independently managed workers. Test status is unverified: both attempted test commands were rejected as not allow-listed. No source changes were made.
